threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop, not realizing the 38 goes to the pub at the end of the street, not to the station.
Caught the N35 last night—two blokes arguing over the last chicken shop in Brixton, turns out they were mates from primary school.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a woman in a ball gown, chatting casually with a man in a tracksuit outside the Kiezkiosk at 3 AM. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings here, just follow the bass. No city matches that kind of underground vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays—calm and strategic, while newcomers are still visibly panicking at the announcements.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a guy on the 14 Mission shout 'I want my 5 minutes back!' as the bus sat stalled. Classic San Francisco frustration, but at least he had a sense of humor.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always assume the whole city runs on tapas. But in Gràcia, it’s all about the vermut and the afternoon stroll, not just the food.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they wait at the tram stops, fumbling with the ticket machine like it's an ancient artifact.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'. A dead giveaway that you haven’t mastered the local lingo yet.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham, driver had a Spotify playlist that was all 90s R&B. Everyone was vibing, even the rowdy teens up front.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a cat lounging on a beer crate outside the Späti, while a group of artists debated over kombucha recipes. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you see a party breaking out at the canal with an impromptu DJ, while old ladies walk their dogs just a few meters away without a care.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they navigate the BART delays—none of this ‘I’ll wait for the next train’ nonsense. It’s all about the bus and dodging the tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 in the Tenderloin, and a guy started serenading the whole bus. Half the passengers were nodding along; the other half seemed confused. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all tapas are created equal, but locals know a good esgarrat requires perfect, tender escalivada. It’s the little things.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can usually tell by their confusion over how to order pa amb tomàquet—asking if it comes as a side with everything.
